g.text: The state of a table buffer

div.p: csv.State, one per buffer. The file's columns, and everything the user has asked for on top of them.

tr.td: Every source column, in display order, hidden ones among them
The row id the pipeline prepends, column_id -1
The anchor cell, the head cell and the kind

div.p: What a column is: name as the file spells it, a unique label, column_id, hidden. A repeated name takes a [n] suffix in its label, so rename can address it.
Also which columns the table draws. display_columns takes the visible ones from state.columns. Hide, cut, paste and swap all work on that one list.
From a 600 row sample: int, float with a decimal count, date, or text. The user can override the width, the alignment and the printf spec.
csv.Selection: an anchor cell, a head cell, and a kind saying which of the two axes those cells bound. row takes every column, column takes every row.
buffer.render clears it, so both ends belong to the layout on screen.
movement.lua is what moves the head: a shift keyed move, or any move made while nvim is in a visual mode.
